headline: AI companies say computer-simulated trials can predict whether a drug will succeed in a real trial.
score_reason: Lowered from 7 to 6: the track record is the company's own figure, and the same report includes a miss.
importance_line: What is new: AI firms say computer simulations can forecast trial results and help drugmakers decide which drugs to push forward, which matters first to patients who join trials that may fail and then to drugmakers, and the honest doubt is that the five-in-six record is the company's own figure and the same report includes a miss.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by The Independent, that BioinvestGPT, a Copenhagen-based AI company, says it has correctly predicted five of six trial outcomes so far, including the failed del-desiran trial from Novartis. The same report notes a miss, an AI forecast of a positive result for Novartis's pelacarsen that was followed by a failed late-stage trial, and quotes experts who say human trials remain necessary.
notes: Reuters original blocked (HTTP 401); text read on The Independent, which says BioinvestGPT shared its analyses with Reuters. Wire credit to be confirmed by the editor (see facts notes). Company claims are labelled as the company's.
